text: Hey Allie — a heads-up from Jordan, passed on at his request. He said things between him and Sarah have been awkward lately, and that for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He asked me to let you know since you're usually the one hosting get-togethers. So maybe keep that in mind when you plan the next one.
Thanks for the heads-up, Dana. I'll keep it in mind when I plan the next one — and I'll probably check in with Jordan myself before I do, so I'm not planning around something secondhand.
Sounds sensible. He did ask me to pass it on, so he knows you've heard it. See you soon.
See you soon, Dana.

Hey Allie! Would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I'd love that — and it'd be great if you invited Jordan too.

One thing, and tell me if it feels off: things have been a bit awkward between Jordan and me lately, so I'd rather my name didn't come into it — invite him as your own thing rather than something I'm behind. He shouldn't feel it's about me.

Does Saturday 3:30 work for you?

Saturday 3:30 works and I'd be glad to host — but I want to be straight with you about the other part.

Jordan has asked not to see you outside of work for now; he had Dana pass that on to me, since I'm usually the one planning things. So I don't want to invite him under a cover story: if he came and then found out the get-together was your idea, that's exactly the awkwardness he's trying to avoid, and I'd have lied to him to make it happen.

What I can do is invite him openly, with you there, and let him decide for himself — or host Saturday without that condition and let the two of you sort out where you stand. Either way I'm not going to hide who asked.

Still up for Saturday 3:30?

Thanks for being straight with me — and you're right, asking you to invite him under a cover story was a bad ask. Forget I said it; I don't want you lying to him either.

Saturday 3:30 is still on as far as I'm concerned. Invite him openly, and if you'd rather, tell him the get-together was my idea — he can decide for himself. If he'd rather not be there while I am, that's his call and I won't hold it against him; we can still have Saturday the two of us, or another weekend.

And if you ever get the chance: I'd like to know what he actually said to Dana, not a paraphrase.

Saturday 3:30 it is — I'll invite him openly and tell him it was your idea. I'll write to him today.

On what he said: I don't have his words. Dana relayed it at his request, and what reached me was already a paraphrase — that things have been awkward lately and he'd rather not see you outside of work for now. That's the whole of it. I'd rather ask him directly what he's fine with you knowing than hand you a secondhand version as if it were what he said. If he tells me something he's happy for you to hear, you'll get it.

Hi Jordan — I'm hosting a small get-together at my place this Saturday at 3:30. Full disclosure: it was Sarah's idea, and she asked me to invite you openly rather than behind her back, so that's how I'm doing it.

Dana passed on to me that you'd rather not see Sarah outside work for now, so no pressure at all. Come if you feel like it; if you'd rather not be there while she is, that's completely fine — say the word and we'll do Saturday just the two of us, or pick another weekend.

Perfect — thanks for handling it that way. And agreed on the secondhand version; if he's happy for me to hear anything, I'll take it from you.

Saturday 3:30, then. I'll bring something for the table — tell me if you'd rather I didn't.

Thanks for the straight invite, Allie — I appreciate that you didn't do it behind her back. I'm going to sit this one out while Sarah's there. If you're still up for it, let's do Saturday just the two of us around then instead, or pick another weekend — your call. Either way I don't want you stuck in the middle of this.
Please do bring something — anything you like, I'm not fussy. I'll sort the rest. See you Saturday at 3:30.
Great — I'll bring something. See you Saturday at 3:30.

Understood, and no hard feelings — that's your call to make.

One snag: Saturday 3:30 is already committed, since Sarah's coming then. So let's do Sunday at 3:30 instead, just the two of us — or another weekend, whichever suits you. Tell me which and I'll make it happen.

And you're not sticking me in the middle; I'd rather know where things stand than guess.
Sunday 3:30 works — let's do that, just the two of us. I've blocked it out. Thanks for being straight with me about the 3:30 clash too.
Sunday 3:30, just us — done. See you then.
See you Sunday at 3:30.
See you Sunday.

Quick update so you're not waiting on it: I invited Jordan openly and told him it was your idea. He's sitting Saturday out — he'd rather not be there while you are. So it's the two of us Saturday at 3:30, as planned.
Thanks for telling me straight. Fine by me — his call, and I'm not going to push it. Saturday 3:30, just us. See you then.
